facts.statement: Oraristrix brea, the La Brea owl, is an extinct owl found in the Upper Pleistocene asphalt deposits of the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles, California.
facts.quote: Oraristrix brea, commonly known as the La Brea owl, is an extinct species of owl reported from the Upper Pleistocene asphalt deposits at the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles, California.

facts.statement: The species was first described by Hildegarde Howard in 1933 as Strix brea before being moved to the genus Oraristrix by Campbell and Bocheński in 2010.
facts.quote: It was first described by Hildegarde Howard in 1933 as Strix brea and was subsequently assigned to the separate genus Oraristrix by Campbell and Bocheński in 2010.

facts.statement: Fossils of this species have also been found in Upper Pleistocene asphalt deposits at Carpinteria, California.
facts.quote: The species has also been recorded from Upper Pleistocene asphalt deposits of Carpinteria, California.

facts.statement: Oraristrix brea likely had more terrestrial habits than modern North American owls of the genera Bubo and Strix, indicated by its relatively long legs compared to its wingspan.
facts.quote: Its relatively long legs in proportion to its wingspan suggest that O. brea was more terrestrial in its habits than modern North American species of Bubo and Strix.

facts.statement: Oraristrix belongs to the family Strigidae.
Oraristrix lived from the Chibanian to the Late Pleistocene, between 0.21 and 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chibanian to Late Pleistocene (0.21 to 0.0117 million years ago)
